To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reflection and transmission coefficient of a surface wave train over a varying sea-bed is dependent on the shape of the undulation and the Bragg resonance.

the reflection of surface waves by a patch of uneven bottom can be predicted with reasonable accuracy by the use of linear water wave theory, and the reflection coefficient becomes large when Bragg resonance takes place.
the scattering coefficients of surface waves over a varying sinusoidal undulating sea-bed are evaluated and presented in graphical form.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reflection and transmission of a train of surface waves over a small undulation in the bottom.
the problem of the scattering of a surface water wave by a small undulating sea-bed.
the problem of scattering of waves by a small patch of uneven sea bed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present analysis provides a good understanding of the scattering of surface waves by a small patch of undulation of the sea bottom, and it can be applied to the study of scattering of surface waves from any type of undulating sea bottom.

the reflection coefficient for the bottom undulation with varying sinusoidal shape function has been evaluated for a wide range of parameters, and that the reflection coefficient is a multiple of the total number of ripples present in the patch, which is in agreement with the results of the available literature.

the reflection coefficient for a varying sinusoidal bottom is a multiple of the ripple number, and the reflection coefficient for the case of a varying sinusoidal undulation of the sea bottom is given in terms of the reflection coefficient for one ripple, and the ripple number, which is the number of rippers in the patch.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present work is a significant improvement on the earlier works and it is expected to find wide application in the field of wave propagation.
the reflection and transmission of surface waves over a small patch of an uneven sea bed are investigated and the results are presented for some special shape functions.
, in the case of a single ripple in the patch, we obtain the results in the literature and for multiple ripples we present new results.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scattering of waves by the uneven sea bottom can be a major source of reflection and hence, a major contributor to wave energy loss.
the reflection coefficient is not sensitive to the shape function of the bottom undulation, but is sensitive to the number of ruffles in the patch.
the scattering of surface waves over uneven sea bed is highly dependent on the shape of the undulation.
